items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
notes: No disclosure of pecuniary interest was declared by any member of Council at this point in the meeting.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
notes: That the previous meeting minutes be approved.

items.title: WR Community Energy
notes: Matthew Day, Executive Director, WR Community Energy gave a presentation outlining the energy resiliency of the Region, detailing the use, waste, and demand of energy within the Region. He then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Consent Motion
notes: That consent motion items (a) through (f) be approved.

items.title: Items Removed From the Consent Motion
Award of RFT25-10 – AMCC Renovation,
notes: Heather Liddycoat gave a presentation outlining the scope of the work for the renovation, as well as some of the design and accessibility elements for the washroom renovation. She then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Albert McCormick Community Centre
notes: Heather Liddycoat gave a presentation detailing the background of the project, including community engagement, as well as the design features of the new library space and community room. She then responded to questions of Council. Brad Witzel also responded to questions of Council.

Frank Mensink, Board Chair, Waterloo Public Library Board gave a presentation offering details on the library demographics for 2024, as well as an overview of the community engagement. Nicole Campbell, Board Member, Waterloo Public Library Board continued the presentation explaining the community uses for the future space. Frank Mensink responded to questions of Council. Kevin Van Ooteghem and Brad Witzel also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Allocation of 2024 Surplus
notes: Paul Hettinga offered some introductory remarks outlining the surplus and the recommendations of the report. He then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Canada Housing Infrastructure
notes: Prepared By: Dan Ditaranto and Brad Witzel

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
notes: No disclosure of pecuniary interest was declared by any member of Council at this point in the meeting.

items.title: Official Plan Amendment No. 57 and
notes: Aminu Bello gave a presentation providing an overview of the proposed development, detailing the Zoning By-law and Official Plan amendments being requested. He then responded to questions of Council.

Courtney Fish, Senior Planner, KLM Planning Partners Inc. gave a presentation further outlining the proposed development, and offered additional site context. She then responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application is now open to Council for a motion and debate.

items.title: Questions
notes: Mayor McCabe asked Nicole Papke, Acting Commissioner of Community Services, a question regarding the possibility of a temporary leash-free dog park in Uptown as discussed a few months before, and if there was a status update. Nicole Papke responded that staff were aware of Council and the community’s interest to see this.

She added that it was her understand in that there could be a report coming to Council in June, 2025 with some recommendations. Nicole Papke informed Council that the Waterloo Park Advisory Committee was engaged prior to the report being submitted.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Roach congratulated Taylor Elgersma, former Wilfrid Laurier Golden Hawks quarterback, who was signed to the Green Bay Packers. He is the fourth quarterback from a Canadian University signed to the NFL.

Mayor McCabe highlighted some information from the Region. They’re currently working on their long-term waste management strategy, which is a 25-year strategy that they’re looking to develop. There are two virtual meetings on May 14th and May 15th. Residents can check EngageWR for details about ongoing engagement during the summer.

Mayor McCabe also mentioned that the Children and Youth Planning Table and Smart Waterloo Region are receiving pitches for the Youth Impact Project, for youth looking to make positive change in their communities. Ideas can receive up to $5,000.
Councillor Roe mentioned that the Waterloo Region District School Board held a multilingual speech competition this past Friday, May 9 at Waterloo Collegiate Institute.
The Mayor was also in attendance for a portion of it. It was exciting to see newcomers engage in the competition, making friends and adapting to the school.

motions.text: 1. That Council approve report CORP2025-015. 2. That as part of report CORP2025-015 Council acknowledges a 2024 property-tax base surplus of $2,659,662. 3. That Council approve $500,000 of the 2024 year-end property-tax base surplus be allocated to the Planning Litigation Reserve Fund as recommended via CORP2024-034 - Reserves and Reserve Funds Annual Update. 4. That Council approve $250,000 of the 2024 year-end property-tax base surplus be allocated to the Cemetery Reserve Fund as recommended via COM2024-043 - Cemetery Services 2025 Fees and Charges. 5. That Council approve the remaining 2024 year-end property-tax base surplus of $1,909,662 to be allocated to the following reserves as per the Surplus Allocation Policy (Appendix A): 1) $477,416 to the Tax Rate Stabilization Reserve (TRS) 2) $477,416 to the Capital Infrastructure Reinvestment Reserve Fund (CIRRF) 3) $477,415 to the Climate Action Reserve Fund (CARF) 4) $477,415 to the Library Expansion and Rehabilitation Reserve Fund (LXPR) 6. That Council approve that any adjustments as a result of the year- end audit to the final surplus figure be transferred to/from the TRS (25%), CIRRF (25%), CARF (25%) and the LXPR (25%) in compliance with the Surplus Allocation Policy (FC-003).
motions.text_html:
1. That Council approve report CORP2025-015.

2. That as part of report CORP2025-015 Council acknowledges a 2024 property-tax base surplus of $2,659,662.

3. That Council approve $500,000 of the 2024 year-end property-tax base surplus be allocated to the Planning Litigation Reserve Fund as recommended via CORP2024-034 - Reserves and Reserve Funds Annual Update.

4. That Council approve $250,000 of the 2024 year-end property-tax base surplus be allocated to the Cemetery Reserve Fund as recommended via COM2024-043 - Cemetery Services 2025 Fees and Charges.

5. That Council approve the remaining 2024 year-end property-tax base surplus of $1,909,662 to be allocated to the following reserves as per the Surplus Allocation Policy (Appendix A): 1) $477,416 to the Tax Rate Stabilization Reserve (TRS) 2) $477,416 to the Capital Infrastructure Reinvestment Reserve Fund (CIRRF) 3) $477,415 to the Climate Action Reserve Fund (CARF) 4) $477,415 to the Library Expansion and Rehabilitation Reserve Fund (LXPR)

6. That Council approve that any adjustments as a result of the year- end audit to the final surplus figure be transferred to/from the TRS (25%), CIRRF (25%), CARF (25%) and the LXPR (25%) in compliance with the Surplus Allocation Policy (FC-003).

motions.text: 1. That Council approve IPPW2025-028. 2. That Council formally approve the City of Waterloo’s grant submission to the Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund (CHIF) grant for the Laurel Creek Sanitary Pumping Station and Conservation Drive Sanitary Pumping Station located in Beaver Creek Meadows in the amount of $21,073,000 with the CHIF grant funding up to $8,429,000. 3. That should the City of Waterloo’s grant submission to the Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund (CHIF) be successful, Council authorize the Mayor and Clerk to sign the grant transfer payment agreement(s) and any other related documents, in a form subject to the satisfaction of the City Solicitor. 4. That should the City’s Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund (CHIF) grant application be successful, Council direct staff to proceed with tendering the Laurel Creek Sanitary Pumping Station and the Conservation Drive Sanitary Pumping Station project in the fall of 2025. 5. That should the Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund (CHIF) grant application not be successful, Council direct staff to continue negotiations with the developer group regarding a suitable risk sharing approach for the two pumping stations, subject to the satisfaction of the Commissioner of IPPW.
motions.text_html:
1. That Council approve IPPW2025-028.

2. That Council formally approve the City of Waterloo’s grant submission to the Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund (CHIF) grant for the Laurel Creek Sanitary Pumping Station and Conservation Drive Sanitary Pumping Station located in Beaver Creek Meadows in the amount of $21,073,000 with the CHIF grant funding up to $8,429,000.

3. That should the City of Waterloo’s grant submission to the Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund (CHIF) be successful, Council authorize the Mayor and Clerk to sign the grant transfer payment agreement(s) and any other related documents, in a form subject to the satisfaction of the City Solicitor.

4. That should the City’s Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund (CHIF) grant application be successful, Council direct staff to proceed with tendering the Laurel Creek Sanitary Pumping Station and the Conservation Drive Sanitary Pumping Station project in the fall of 2025.

5. That should the Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund (CHIF) grant application not be successful, Council direct staff to continue negotiations with the developer group regarding a suitable risk sharing approach for the two pumping stations, subject to the satisfaction of the Commissioner of IPPW.
